Classification: Bloodline (pagan, @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.zCWdD1NpOCn03CwE]{Gangrel}-adjacent)

Often mistaken for a @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.zCWdD1NpOCn03CwE]{Gangrel} subspecies, the Lhiannan (or Druids) are wild, fey creatures bound to a woodland spirit joined to the body of a vampire long ago by a shadowy figure called the Crone. As Christian forces stamp out or assimilate the old religions, the Lhiannan are pushed further from civilization, and their bloodline is slowly dying: the spirit that empowers them weakens and divides each time a Lhiannan sires a childe, so elders sire only rarely, hoarding what remains of the spirit's power. Lhiannan are fiercely territorial and strongly tied to forests, growing uncomfortable or ill in cities. The Gangrel bear them intense hatred for reasons elders only vaguely allude to as a "great betrayal."

Disciplines: Animalism, Ogham, Presence

Advantage: Mortals who follow the pagan ways form a Herd from which a Lhiannan may gain one Blood Trait per level of Ogham possessed (15 minutes out of play per Trait). Lhiannan begin play with one Trait each in Occult and Hearth Wisdom.

Disadvantage: Attempts to determine a Lhiannan's supernatural nature via Auspex or other means gain a two-Trait bonus, as their inhuman aura unsettles anyone nearby. A Lhiannan who leaves her territory suffers a one-Trait penalty for each week she remains away, resetting only after returning and resting in her territory for a few hours.

Organization: Scattered, isolated guardians of surviving pagan enclaves, with no central leadership; each jealously guards her own shard of the bloodline's founding spirit.

Suggested Viae: Beast; a few follow the Roads of Kings or Sin.
